stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 4 \ln\left(1 + \frac{x + 3}{3}\right) \). The Taylor series for f about \( x = -3 \) is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{4 (-1)^{n+1} \left(x + 3\right)^{n}}{n \cdot 3^{n}} \). Does the series converge to f at \( x = 0 \)? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: Yes, because \( x = 0 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( -6 < x \le 0 \) includes.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x + 3\right| < 3 \), the interior \( -6 < x < 0 \), and \( x = 0 \) is an endpoint.
At \( x = 0 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{4 (-1)^{n+1}}{n} \), which converges by the alternating series test, so the interval of convergence is \( -6 < x \le 0 \).
Yes, because \( x = 0 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( -6 < x \le 0 \) includes.
